components: a long diagonal down to the lower left
a small hump that rises from it and comes back down
a curve that rounds the foot and rises to the right
strokeOrder: begin at the top and cut down to the lower left, then without lifting climb back up the same line, turn over the small hump and down, and swing round the foot and up to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03093 file records ん as a single stroke path in this order and direction: the diagonal, the climb back up it, the hump, then the rising finish; so there are no pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03093.svg, hiragana ん (U+3093 HIRAGANA LETTER N), one stroke path kvg:03093-s1 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores ん as one directed path in writing order: it starts at the top, cuts down to the lower left, turns back up the same line, arches over a small hump, comes down, rounds the foot and rises to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. In the print glyph the hump leaves the diagonal partway up, so the path goes down to the tip of the diagonal and climbs back up that ink to the branch before turning over the hump.

notes: The only hiragana that is a bare consonant, and it still takes a full beat of its own.
